tagline: Thirty-three miles of county dirt along a row of old volcanoes.
intro: County Road 42 leaves NM 53 on its south side and goes off into El Malpais on dirt and gravel, 33 miles across the badlands to NM 117. It forms the western boundary of the West Malpais Wilderness, and more than a dozen old cinder cones run north and south beside it as the Chain of Craters.
There is no water and no restroom along the road. The nearest food, gas and water are in Grants, about 27 miles off.

moments.title: Continental Divide Trail
moments.text: About five miles south of NM 53 a rock cairn marks the trail, which winds among the Chain of Craters for some 20 miles to a second trailhead on the same road.

moments.title: Hole-in-the-Wall
moments.text: A trailhead off the byway is the start of a hike of several miles over open plains and lava to a 6,700-acre island of ponderosa pine and open range with lava all around it.

practical: County Road 42 is an unpaved dirt road with blind curves and hills; BLM recommends a high-clearance vehicle, and the road is likely to be impassable when wet. There is no water or restroom along it.
